name: LIS3DH Accelerometer
description: The `lis3dh` motion platform allows you to use your LIS3DH 3-axis accelerometer ([datasheet](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/lis3dh.pdf)) with ESPHome. The [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c/) is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the sensor. Defaults to `0x18`; on boards where the SDO/SA0 pin is tied high it is `0x19`.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval at which sensor data is read. Defaults to `250ms`.

config_entries.label: Accelerometer Odr
config_entries.description: The output data rate of the accelerometer. One of `1HZ`, `10HZ`, `25HZ`, `50HZ`, `100HZ`, `200HZ`, `400HZ`, `1620HZ`, `1344HZ`. Defaults to `100HZ`. `1620HZ` needs `operating_mode: LOW_POWER`, and `1344HZ` is rejected in that mode because the chip would then run at 5376 Hz.

config_entries.label: Accelerometer Range
config_entries.description: The full-scale range of the accelerometer. One of `2G`, `4G`, `8G`, `16G`. Defaults to `2G`. A smaller range gives finer resolution; a larger range measures stronger accelerations.

config_entries.label: Axis Map
config_entries.description: Remap or invert the physical axes of the sensor to match your board orientation. Each key (`x`, `y`, `z`) maps to the physical axis it should read from, optionally prefixed with `-` to invert. All three axes must be present and each physical axis may only appear once. Mutually exclusive with `transform_matrix`.

config_entries.label: Interrupt
config_entries.description: Configure the on-chip motion (activity) interrupt. When present, the LIS3DH drives one of its physical INT pads whenever the acceleration crosses the threshold. See [Motion Wake-Up](https://esphome.io/components/motion/lis3dh/#motion-wake-up) below.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: Which physical interrupt pad to drive, `INT1` or `INT2`. Defaults to `INT1`.

config_entries.label: Active High
config_entries.description: The polarity of the interrupt pad. `true` = the pad goes high when the interrupt is active, `false` = it goes low. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Axes
config_entries.description: Which axes may trigger the interrupt, any of `x`, `y`, `z`. Defaults to all three.

config_entries.label: Duration
config_entries.description: How long the threshold must be exceeded before the interrupt fires. It is rounded to whole samples at the selected `accelerometer_odr` and can be at most 127 samples (for example `1270ms` at `100HZ`). Defaults to `0ms`.

config_entries.label: High Pass Filter
config_entries.description: Apply the high-pass filter to the interrupt so the standing gravity component is removed from the threshold comparison, letting you use a small threshold (the change in acceleration). The reported acceleration values are not affected. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Latched
config_entries.description: If `true`, the interrupt stays asserted until the interrupt source register is read (which happens automatically on the next boot). If `false`, the pad follows the motion. Defaults to `true`. For deep-sleep wake-up, `false` is often preferable so the device can return to sleep once movement stops.

config_entries.label: Threshold
config_entries.description: The acceleration above which the interrupt fires. Defaults to `1.1g`. Each enabled axis is compared separately against this value. At rest the axis aligned with gravity reads about 1 g, so with all axes enabled the threshold should stay above `1g`; a value of `1g` or less without `high_pass_filter` is accepted but logs a warning, since gravity alone may then keep the interrupt asserted. Enable `high_pass_filter` to compare against the *change* in acceleration instead, which allows much smaller values. The value cannot exceed what the selected `accelerometer_range` can represent (about `2g` at `2G`, `4g` at `4G`, `7.9g` at `8G` and `23.6g` at `16G`).

config_entries.label: Operating Mode
config_entries.description: Selects the resolution, which also affects power usage. One of `LOW_POWER` (8-bit), `NORMAL` (10-bit), `HIGH_RESOLUTION` (12-bit). Defaults to `HIGH_RESOLUTION`.

config_entries.label: Transform Matrix
config_entries.description: A 3×3 transformation matrix applied to raw accelerometer and gyroscope readings. This allows arbitrary calibration beyond simple axis remapping. Can be specified as a flat list of 9 values (row-major order) or as a 3×3 nested list. Mutually exclusive with `axis_map`. The matrix can be obtained from the runtime calibration actions described below — after calibration the computed matrix is logged in a format that can be copied directly into your configuration for persistent use.
